forces.title: Softening interest rate tailwinds impact bank net interest income
forces.description: The elevated interest rate environment, which previously drove strong growth in net interest income (NII) for banks, is now softening. As interest rates ease, net interest margins (NIMs) are expected to dampen, leading to a moderation in NII growth. This shift will necessitate banks to increase focus on fee-based revenues and operational discipline to sustain profitability, impacting overall earnings for commercial and retail banking.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI threatens deposit yields and credit card revenues
forces.description: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to significantly reshape banking economics. Autonomous software agents can optimize account yields by sweeping idle cash to higher-yielding products and dynamically route credit card transactions to minimize fees or maximize rewards. This directly puts retail and commercial deposit net interest income and consumer credit card revenues at risk, compelling banks to adapt their strategies for value capture in these core Commercial & Retail Banking areas.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Payment infrastructure fragmentation and A2A competition challenges cards
forces.description: The global payment infrastructure is fragmenting into regional, multi-rail competitive arenas rather than converging. Zero-fee domestic real-time account-to-account (A2A) networks are emerging, directly competing with legacy card perimeters and threatening traditional credit card business models in card-resilient markets like Western Europe. This 'head-on collision' requires banks to navigate complex structural divergences and protect interchange revenue, potentially leading to margin compression on card-related fees.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Higher interest rates suppress Belgian mortgage lending demand
forces.description: Long-term interest rates have continued to rise, leading to restrictive financing conditions in Belgium. This directly impacts the Commercial & Retail Banking sector by weakening mortgage production and overall demand for new mortgages. The number of new mortgages in Belgium was already 10% below the previous year's level in the first eight months of 2026, indicating sustained pressure on lending volumes and potential revenue for banks.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Disintermediation risk for commercial banks from agentic treasury management
forces.description: Agentic treasury management is an emerging commercial opportunity but also poses a significant disintermediation risk for commercial banks. Independent platforms are building autonomous treasury agents for SMEs that source liquidity and rails dynamically, potentially commoditizing banks into utility providers if third-party software agents hold the client mandate. This 'ERP-to-bank inversion' necessitates transaction banks to deploy proprietary agentic advisory capabilities to retain client relationships and avoid becoming mere balance sheet providers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Geopolitical and regulatory fragmentation hinders payment rail innovation
forces.description: Geopolitical tensions and national supervisory frameworks are becoming the primary pacing variables for payment rail innovation. Major markets, including Europe, are pursuing paths to preserve monetary sovereignty, leading to regulatory divergence rather than convergence towards global standards. This fragmentation creates challenges for financial services providers navigating cross-border transactions and determining legal/financial responsibility for autonomous failures, impacting the efficiency and scalability of payment services offered by Commercial & Retail Banking.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Shift towards fee-based structures due to low interest rates in EMEA
forces.description: In the EMEA region, lower interest rates are compressing treasury and deposit margins, prompting a rapid and structural shift in banking revenue models towards fee-based structures. This change requires Commercial & Retail Banking institutions to increasingly monetize value-added software, fraud mitigation, and specialized treasury services alongside baseline processing to sustain revenue growth, as dependence on net interest income diminishes. This affects the core profitability drivers for banks in the region.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Rising energy prices drive demand for energy-efficient homes
forces.description: The current environment of higher energy prices reinforces the trend of consumers valuing energy-efficient housing. This creates a specific segment of resilient demand within the housing market, as energy efficiency reduces expenses, hedges against future price shocks, and meets stricter renovation standards. For Commercial & Retail Banking, this could mean sustained demand for mortgages and financing solutions for energy-efficient properties, or green mortgages, potentially offsetting some of the broader market slowdown.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Payments revenue growth moderating, shifting towards operational excellence and fee-based structures
viewpoints.description: Global payments revenue growth is moderating from 9% to 4% annually, signaling a structural transition. In EMEA, lower interest rates are compressing treasury and deposit margins, driving a rapid shift to fee-based structures. Growth is projected to slow to 3% annually in 2025-30 from 14% in 2020-25. Performance will depend less on broad market momentum and more on commercial excellence, operational discipline, and technological leadership, with greater emphasis on fee resilience and yield discipline for banks.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market resilience masks a challenging outlook amid higher interest rates
viewpoints.description: The Belgian housing market showed unexpected resilience in Q2 2026 with modest price increases and transaction recovery. However, this masks a challenging outlook, as weaker mortgage production and sustained higher interest rates suggest demand will lose momentum. Financing conditions are expected to remain restrictive, impacting mortgage lending and potentially slowing house price growth in the coming years. Demand for energy-efficient homes is expected to remain relatively resilient due to rising energy prices and stricter renovation standards.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI and digital assets threaten traditional bank deposit and card revenues
viewpoints.description: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and digital assets such as stablecoins are poised to disrupt traditional banking revenue streams. Agentic AI can automate deposit sweeps to higher-yielding accounts and optimize credit card usage to avoid fees, putting significant deposit net interest income and card revenues at risk. Stablecoins can bypass traditional interchange and FX markups, shifting float income away from commercial bank deposits. This indicates a material reshape of bank profit pools, well before the full scale of disruption is evident against total industry revenue.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.description: Software agents automatically sweep idle cash to higher-yielding accounts and investment products, causing balance migration and reducing bank net interest income from deposits.
Agentic AI can lead to payment rail substitution, automated repayment optimization, fee avoidance, and real-time foreign-exchange routing, reducing consumer credit card revenues.

market_sizing.methodology: Baseline adoption scenario for agentic AI's impact on global payments revenue; covers retail and commercial deposits and consumer credit card revenues. Represents 4% of the $1.9 trillion pool of these revenues.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

demand_drivers.description: Rising energy prices and stricter renovation standards increase the value premium for energy-efficient homes, supporting their demand despite overall market cooling.

pnl_drivers.description: Increased long-term interest rates lead to restrictive financing conditions, dampening mortgage demand and new mortgage production, impacting bank lending income.
